slides.subtitle:
Eastbank to Westhaven, 17:00-20:00
An invented urban ferry story, not a ridership forecast.
slides.notes: Eastbank and Westhaven are fictional places in this case. Serif headlines establish an editorial voice. No photographed place, external visual asset, quotation, or license is used. The route is one-way in this analysis.

slides.title: A queue becomes the evening's clock
slides.subtitle: Three moments in the synthetic baseline, not eyewitness reporting

milestones.title: Seats go unused
milestones.body: The first release boards 40 of 80 places. Spare seats cannot be carried forward.

milestones.title: The wave arrives
milestones.body: The 18:30-19:00 interval adds 145 arrivals. After boarding, 95 people remain in the queue.

milestones.title: The count is unfinished
milestones.body: 425 people have boarded; 115 remain. The model has no later service or abandonment.

slides.caption: SYN-F1. Simplified end-of-interval seat release, FIFO queue, empty initial queue. Moments describe one invented representative evening; they do not measure individual waiting times.
slides.notes: Each 30-minute slot ends with the stated release. Baseline releases are at 17:30, 18:00, 18:30, 19:00, 19:30, and 20:00. This abstraction deliberately omits within-interval arrivals and exact departure headways.

slides.title: The middle hour carries 47% of arrivals
slides.subtitle: Synthetic representative evening; arrivals are not completed boardings

options.catAxisTitle: Arrival interval; seats released at interval end
options.valAxisTitle: People or offered places per 30 min

slides.caption: SYN-F1. Ten deliberately identical evenings are a constructed case, not a sampled estimate. Six 80-place releases offer 480 places per evening. No day-to-day variability or uncertainty interval is implied.
slides.notes: All ten evenings use the same arrivals, so the per-evening mean equals this representative profile by construction. Arrival records are people presenting once per evening; the case does not identify unique individuals across evenings.

slides.title: Move one release, not the whole promise
slides.subtitle: Synthetic experiment: the same 480 places, distributed differently

left.title: Even spacing
bullets: Six releases of 80 places; one after every interval.

right.title: One release moved to 19:00
bullets: 480 boardings; no unused places in this model.
60 people remain; the first queue rises to 40.

slides.verdict: 55 more boardings per evening, but no added places and no elimination of the queue.
slides.notes: This is an offered-seat allocation test, not an operationally validated timetable. Two releases in one slot may need a second vessel or a different rotation. Crew, berth, return-leg, accessibility, and weather constraints are not modeled. Both columns share the same demand and denominator.

slides.title: The queue shrinks, but does not disappear
slides.subtitle: Synthetic end-of-interval people still waiting, on the same evening

table.caption: SYN-F1/F2. Queue = max(0, prior queue + arrivals - offered places). Peak sampled queue falls from 120 to 65, but early service worsens. Within-interval peak queues and waiting times are unknown.

slides.notes: Moved offered places by interval: 0, 80, 80, 160, 80, 80. All counts are per evening. Baseline boardings: 40, 65, 80, 80, 80, 80. Moved boardings: 0, 80, 80, 160, 80, 80. No passenger abandonment or suppressed demand is assumed.

slides.title: Test the wave, protect the early rider
slides.subtitle: A synthetic planning conclusion, not a service-change authorization
bullets: Check vessel, berth, crew, and return-leg feasibility before any trial.
Measure arrivals, boardings, and timestamped waits separately; keep early riders in the evaluation.
The remaining 60 people require another answer: more capacity, later service, or a different design.
slides.summary_callout: Re-timing addresses 55 of the 115 queued people in this case; it cannot serve all 540 with 480 places.
sources: SYN-F1/F2 | all places, counts, and plans invented
slides.notes: SYN-F1 is the invented demand and baseline. SYN-F2 is the invented moved-release scenario. These source IDs are internal, not external citations. Ten identical evenings yield baseline 4,250 boardings and moved 4,800 boardings, a difference of 550; no causal field result or forecast is asserted.
